learningObjective: Connect a target node's graph neighborhood to the corresponding row of normalized adjacency, then trace how that row aggregates node features before the shared linear transform and activation.
mediumRationale: A deterministic SVG is the smallest medium that can align the same four nodes in graph space, one normalized adjacency row, the matching feature column, and a numeric GCN update. The worked row makes the otherwise abstract A-hat H W multiplication spatial and checkable without interaction.

mediumComparison.svg: Selected: deterministic node geometry, matrix cells, arrows, and a worked calculation connect graph topology to one exact output row in a single responsive figure.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected: an HTML table could represent the adjacency row and arithmetic accessibly, but would not show why its nonzero positions correspond to the target node's one-hop neighborhood.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: switching the target node could demonstrate equivariance, but controls and hidden states are unnecessary for learning the invariant row-to-neighborhood correspondence and would weaken print completeness.

Reuse permission was not relied upon; the four-node cycle, values, layout, labels, and arithmetic are an original worked example.

pages.insight: The graphical-models slide introduces graph factorization and local computation, but it concerns probabilistic inference rather than neural node-feature updates.

The message-passing slide describes probabilistic sum-product messages, forward and backward belief propagation, and EM. The shared term is relevant context, but the mechanism is not GNN neighborhood aggregation or A-hat H W.
The following GMM and HMM slide confirms that the preceding message-passing treatment belongs to latent-variable inference and provides no GNN mechanism.
The preceding rescoring slide ends the language-model section and provides no graph representation or neural message-passing content.
The knowledge-graph embedding slide discusses RESCAL adjacency-tensor factorization, multi-hop relational patterns, and HolE, but not graph convolution or neighborhood aggregation.
The following automatic-speech-recognition title slide marks the end of the knowledge-graph neighborhood and adds no GNN detail.
The preceding slide covers array-sorting algorithms and is unrelated, establishing the boundary before the deck's generic graph data-structure material.

The graph data-structure slide defines adjacency lists and adjacency matrices and explains neighbor lookup and BFS. This supports the topology-to-adjacency-row prerequisite but contains no node features, normalization, learned weights, or GCN.
The following graph-algorithms slide compares traversal and shortest-path algorithms, adding no neural graph computation.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is that each output node corresponds to one row of A-hat: graph edges determine which entries are nonzero, normalization determines their fixed coefficients, H supplies the aligned node features, and W is the learned feature mixer shared across nodes. The original example uses a four-node cycle with self-loops. Every self-added degree is 3, so symmetric normalization gives row B = [1/3, 1/3, 1/3, 0] in A, B, C, D order. With scalar features [3, 0, 6, 9], the aggregate is 3; W = [2, -1] gives [6, -3], and ReLU gives [6, 0]. The arithmetic and drawn neighborhood agree exactly. This equal-degree example is intentionally a mean; on irregular graphs symmetric GCN normalization is a degree-weighted sum and need not sum to one.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed all 214 deck pages and inspected the three closest slide neighborhoods, then checked the primary GCN and message-passing papers, official PyTorch Geometric documentation, and an authoritative Distill exposition before selecting an original numeric neighborhood-to-row SVG.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a linked title and complete description that states the graph edges, target neighborhood, normalized row, input features, and every numeric result. Node labels, borders, matrix positions, a self-loop, arrows, and direct text carry all meaning without color. Its single 360-unit viewBox has no minimum width or horizontal scrolling and scales within the established plot-panel primitive at 390 CSS pixels. Existing theme variables preserve dark-mode contrast, while shared print tokens force a light high-contrast palette and avoid breaks within the figure.
